operator_io_quirks: All 7 tables report rows=0 and every column null_rate/distinct/storage/samples is null/empty: the facts carry NO data profile, so original_values are empty and literal pool must come entirely from TRAIN SQL.
Table name "user" is a SQL keyword; must be double-quoted everywhere (DDL already quotes it).
DDL uses backtick-quoted parent refs (`business`) inside FOREIGN KEY clauses; sqlite_master text must be replayed verbatim.
tip DDL is malformed-ish: missing comma between 'primary key("tip_id")' and 'foreign key(...)' — sqlite accepted it, but line-based unique/check scanning and any re-parse must tolerate it.

FKs point to business.business_id and user.user_id, which are NOT primary keys and NOT declared unique (only bid/uid are PK). Parent columns are non-unique; FK fill draws with replacement from parent values, so duplicates are expected.
business_id / user_id are TEXT but semantically opaque IDs; latitude/longitude are TEXT though numeric-looking; is_open INT is a 0/1 flag; rating REAL in [1,5] semantically.
review.year and tip.year are INT (Number fuzzer, not Date); month is TEXT (String fuzzer) — no date fuzzer dispatches here at all.

No NOT NULL, no CHECK, no UNIQUE constraints anywhere; only PKs. So write_instance_sqlite will rarely skip rows for constraint failures except PK duplicates (already filtered) and the FK-less inserts.
Self-references: none. Cycles: none (business/user are roots; category/checkin/neighbourhood/review/tip are children).
review and tip each have TWO FKs (business_id, user_id) — column order must place both parents before the child.
All PKs are single-column INT (bid, id, uid, cid, id, rid, tip_id) — Number fuzzer with max_l0=inf, so PKs are always fresh draws.
No views, triggers, or indexes in the DDL; empty clone is just the 7 CREATE TABLEs.
operator_ts_expectations: Number fuzzer on every INT/REAL column: uniform in [-10^scale, 10^scale] (scale=0 for INT, 4 for REAL), then +-1/+-2 (int) or +-0.01/+-0.02 (float) perturbation — yields implausible bid/uid/rid, negative review_count, rating outside [1,5], is_open not in {0,1}.

String fuzzer on business_id/user_id/name/city/state/latitude/longitude/month/text: random a-zA-Z0-9() strings length 0..20, plus 50% contaminate (prefix/suffix/drop char) — business_id and user_id become garbage, so FK joins between review/tip and business/user still 'work' (drawn from parent) but the IDs are meaningless.
latitude/longitude declared TEXT -> String fuzzer, so no numeric coordinate semantics; queries comparing them numerically will see random strings.

month TEXT -> String fuzzer, not a month name; year INT -> Number fuzzer, not a plausible year. Any 'month = "January"' or 'year = 2015' literal from TRAIN pool is the only source of plausible values (p=0.2 element reuse).
is_open INT -> Number fuzzer, so values like -3 or 7 appear; queries 'WHERE is_open = 1' will match ~randomly.
rating REAL -> Number fuzzer scale=4, range [-10000,10000] +-0.01 — almost never in [1,5]; 'rating > 4' selects ~half the rows by chance.

FK fill: category/checkin/neighbourhood.business_id drawn from business.business_id (final, after PK/unique filter); review/tip.business_id and .user_id likewise. Since business_id is non-unique in the parent, child rows can share parents — good for joins, but parent business_id values are random strings so no real correlation.
Empty original_values (rows=0) means elements = only literal-pool values; if pool is empty for a column, sampler is pure-fresh (p effectively 1).

Known FN driver: implausible values (negative counts, rating out of range, garbage IDs) make gold predicates like 'rating BETWEEN 1 AND 5' or 'is_open = 1' select wrong cardinalities, so gold and neighbour may agree by accident.

Known FP driver: no ties/duplicates in PKs (filtered) and non-unique FK parents mean GROUP BY / DISTINCT / COUNT(DISTINCT) queries can differ from real data distribution; missing duplicate business_id in business means 'businesses with >1 category' style queries behave differently.
No date fuzzer fires (no date/timestamp declared type), so date-format quirks of TS are not exercised on yelp.
